setup: Seat so the handles line up with mid-chest
Load the same plates on each side
Back on the pad, feet flat
execution: Press the handles out to nearly straight
Keep your shoulder blades on the pad
Let the handles back to a chest stretch
faults: Don't let your shoulders roll forward
Don't lift your back off the pad
Don't slam the arms down between reps

notes: Load and unload plates evenly, one side then the other, so the machine doesn't tip or the arms don't swing.
Set the seat so the start position is a comfortable stretch, not an extreme one.
If pain lingers or comes back, stop this exercise and get it checked by a physio or doctor.
stopIf: Pain that changes how you move

keyPositions.label: Stretch
keyPositions.describe: Seated upright, back on the pad, feet flat. Hands on the handles level with mid-chest, elbows behind the torso line and a little below the shoulders.

keyPositions.label: Press
keyPositions.describe: Handles pressed forward and slightly inward until the arms are nearly straight. Shoulder blades still against the pad, back unchanged.

ikHints: Hands fixed to the handles; handles follow the machine's arc
guideBrief.barPath: Handles travel forward and slightly together on the machine's arc
emphasise: Back and shoulder blades stay on the pad
